exposure: increased vascularity between myometrium and placenta
increased vascularity in the inferior part of the lower uterine segment potentially extending into the parametrial region
outcome: antenatal identification of invasive placentation (placenta accreta, increta, or percreta confirmed at delivery)
cohort: The study included 180 singleton pregnancies with persistent placenta previa and a history of prior cesarean delivery, who were at risk of placenta accreta.
finding: Prenatal ultrasound demonstrates excellent diagnostic accuracy in identifying invasive placentation in women with placenta previa and prior cesarean delivery, with disruption of bladder-myometrial interface being the most sensitive sign and associated with a 73-fold increased risk of placenta accreta.
gest_age: Planned delivery for suspected placenta accreta cases occurred between 34+0 and 35+6 weeks.
